variants.headline: Building project badly behind schedule
variants.sub: Construction of a building project is severely delayed in {colony}.
variants.body:
A building project is badly behind schedule in {colony}. The delay is the established failure against its timetable, not a complete account of why it occurred. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known position from invented shortages, contractor disputes or financial consequences not supplied in the report.

Promises about delivery belong within politics because public purposes require more than an intention on paper. Our movement should insist on responsibility for the distance between a plan and its execution. That principle does not require an invented account of who caused this particular project to fall behind.

We defend {target} against a verdict based on the delay alone. Lateness is established, but its existence does not prove every adverse claim about responsibility or the merits of the project. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.

variants.headline: Construction timetable falls seriously short
